reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the mechanism that a continuous B2 matrix limits ductility and that annealing-induced phase inversion to a BCC matrix with B2 precipitates improves compressive ductility in a specific RHEA. However, the evidence is entirely from compression tests on a different alloy (Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr), so the extension to tensile ductility and to HfZrTiTa0.53 is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Continuous ordered B2 matrix causes poor ductility in RHEAs
Phase inversion to continuous BCC + discrete B2 improves ductility
Controlled annealing can induce this phase inversion
The cited alloy (AlNbTaTiVZr) achieved >20% compressive ductility after inversion
HfZrTiTa0.53 can undergo analogous phase inversion via annealing
